title: botai corpus manifest
description: A declarative description of a course corpus: what to download, what the bytes must hash to, and how a retrieved fragment maps back to a coordinate in a source. Declarative on purpose — the v1 harness ran a Python fetcher shipped inside the course, which made every safety check the course's decision rather than ours. Nothing here executes: the manifest is data, and the downloader is ours.

source_revision.description: The author's publication revision this corpus was built from. Not the local Git HEAD: a corpus describes a published artifact, and tying it to whatever a student happens to have checked out would make the manifest meaningless.

artifacts.description: Downloadable units. An artifact may be an archive (unpacked with limits) or a single file.

url.description: https only. The downloader additionally refuses loopback, link-local, private and metadata addresses, and re-checks every redirect.

sha256.description: Hash of the bytes as served. A mismatch is a hard stop: the artifact is corrupt or the source changed under us.

unpacked_bytes_max.description: Declared ceiling for what this artifact expands to. The downloader enforces it while writing, not only from headers — a zip bomb lies in its headers.

auth_required.description: True when the URL is a private link. The original URL is stored locally only; exports carry a cleaned form.

files.description: The files the corpus must contain after unpacking. Verification is per file: an archive hash proves the archive, not that the file the index refers to is the right one.

kind.description: `none` means text search over the files is the only retrieval method, and the answer says so. It is a legitimate value, not a degraded one.

redistributable.description: null means the manifest does not say. Downloads are still allowed for local study when the learner has legitimate access; redistribution is a separate question.
